a1.say: Let's build Consistent Errors With Problem Details.

a1.cap: Make every error response follow RFC 9457 Problem Details (type, title, status, detail). Map a custom NotFoundException to 404 and validation failures to 400 with a field-to-message map.
a1.say: Make every error response follow RFC 9457 Problem Details (type, title, status, detail). Map a custom Not Found Exception to 404 and validation failures to 400 with a field-to-message map.

lines: Make every error response follow RFC 9457 Problem Details (type, title, status, detail). Map a custom NotFoundException to 404 and validation failures to 400 with a field-to-message map.

a1.cap: Centralise error handling in one @RestControllerAdvice. Each @ExceptionHandler turns an exception into a ProblemDetail, Spring's built-in model of the standard error format.
a1.say: Centralise error handling in one at Rest Controller Advice. Each at Exception Handler turns an exception into a Problem Detail, Spring's built-in model of the standard error format.

a1.cap: Clients then parse one predictable shape, and you never leak stack traces.
@RestControllerAdvice applies these handlers to every controller in the app.
a1.say: at Rest Controller Advice applies these handlers to every controller in the app.

a1.cap: A small domain exception expresses intent: the thing you asked for doesn't exist.
This handler catches it anywhere and answers 404.
ProblemDetail fills in type, title and status for us; we add the human-readable detail.
a1.say: Problem Detail fills in type, title and status for us; we add the human-readable detail.

a1.cap: Failed @Valid checks raise this exception; we translate it into a 400.
a1.say: Failed at Valid checks raise this exception; we translate it into a 400.

a1.cap: We collect each invalid field and its message into a map.
Extra properties are allowed in problem details, so clients get field-level errors.
